subject: Literacy
title: Lines and patterns
objectives: Children will make straight lines, circles and zigzags in sand, paint and on paper.
Children will copy a simple pattern with support.
content: Making straight lines up and down, round and curly patterns, and zigzag and wave patterns in sand, paint and on paper.
teachingActivities: Draw big in the air first, then on large surfaces; say a rhyme for each pattern; never correct pencil grip or correct the direction; let children use whole arm movements; do not teach letter formation.
learnerActivities: Make straight lines, circles and zigzags in sand, paint and on paper and copy a simple pattern with support.
resources: A tray of sand or flour
assessment: Observe whether each child makes straight and round marks on purpose and copies a simple pattern.
expectedOutcomes: Makes straight and round marks on purpose.
crossCurricular: Physical Development: gross and fine motor

lessons.title: Lines up and down
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will make straight lines up and down and across.
successCriteria: Makes a line up and down
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make marks with fingers, chalk and crayons and have been listening to the sounds s, a, t and p.
resources: A ribbon stick for each child
lessons.starter: Draw a straight line in the air from top to bottom and say "Down, down, down." Draw across and say "Across."
teacherActivities: Draw a line in the air and say "up" and "down". Do it slowly.
Give each child a ribbon stick and draw lines in the air.
Draw lines in the sand: down, up and across.
Give crayons and large paper and let the children draw lines.
learnerActivities: Children draw the line in the air with a finger.
Children make lines with the ribbon.
Child makes lines in the sand with a finger.
Child makes lines on paper.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Draw a line in the air and say "up" and "down". Do it slowly. Children: Children draw the line in the air with a finger.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a ribbon stick and draw lines in the air. Children: Children make lines with the ribbon.
Step 3. Teacher: Draw lines in the sand: down, up and across. Children: Child makes lines in the sand with a finger.
Step 4. Teacher: Give crayons and large paper and let the children draw lines. Children: Child makes lines on paper.

practical.title: Line drawing
steps: Draw lines in the air with ribbons.
Make lines in the sand with a finger.
Draw lines on large paper with crayons.
practical.safety: Use ribbon sticks with soft ends and keep children apart. Supervise sand and crayons and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Move the child’s hand to make the line together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to draw five straight lines and count them.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you draw a line down?
Can you draw a line across?

lessons.conclusion: Smooth the sand and wipe hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Draw lines in sand or flour with your child at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make straight lines up and down and across" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Down, down, down, across, across, across.

lessons.title: Circles and curls
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will make round and curly patterns.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make marks with fingers, chalk and crayons and have been listening to the sounds s, a, t and p.
lessons.starter: Draw a big circle in the air and say "Round and round." Draw a curl and say "Curly, curly."
teacherActivities: Draw big circles in the air with your arm and say "Round and round".
Draw a circle in the flour tray with a finger.
Give paint and brushes and let the children paint circles and curls.
Draw a spiral and say "Round and round to the middle."
learnerActivities: Children draw circles in the air.
Child draws a circle in the flour.
Child paints round shapes.
Child copies the spiral with a finger.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Draw big circles in the air with your arm and say "Round and round". Children: Children draw circles in the air.
Step 2. Teacher: Draw a circle in the flour tray with a finger. Children: Child draws a circle in the flour.
Step 3. Teacher: Give paint and brushes and let the children paint circles and curls. Children: Child paints round shapes.
Step 4. Teacher: Draw a spiral and say "Round and round to the middle." Children: Child copies the spiral with a finger.

practical.title: Round and round
practical.safety: Use washable paint and aprons and keep paint off faces. Supervise brushes and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Move the child’s hand in a circle together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to draw a spiral and a circle.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Clean up the paint and look at the circles on the wall.
lessons.homeConnection: Draw circles with a finger in sand or with a crayon at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make round and curly patterns" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Zigzag and wave
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will make zigzag and wave patterns.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make marks with fingers, chalk and crayons and have been listening to the sounds s, a, t and p.
lessons.starter: Draw a zigzag in the air and say "Zig, zag, zig, zag." Draw a wave and say "Up and down like the sea."
teacherActivities: Draw a zigzag in the air and let children copy.
Draw a wave in the air and let children copy.
Draw zigzags and waves with chalk on the ground or on paper.
Wave a scarf like a sea wave and move to music.
learnerActivities: Children draw zigzags in the air.
Children draw waves in the air.
Child draws zigzags and waves.
Children wave the scarf up and down.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Draw a zigzag in the air and let children copy. Children: Children draw zigzags in the air.
Step 2. Teacher: Draw a wave in the air and let children copy. Children: Children draw waves in the air.
Step 3. Teacher: Draw zigzags and waves with chalk on the ground or on paper. Children: Child draws zigzags and waves.
Step 4. Teacher: Wave a scarf like a sea wave and move to music. Children: Children wave the scarf up and down.

practical.title: Zig and wave
steps: Draw zigzags and waves in the air.
Draw them with chalk on a safe surface.
Draw them on large paper with crayons.
practical.safety: Use chalk on a paved area away from roads and wash hands after. Keep scarves soft and children apart.

differentiation.support: Move the child’s hand along the zigzag together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to draw a zigzag and a wave side by side.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What does a wave look like?
questions.expected: Up and down like the sea.

lessons.conclusion: Wave the scarf slowly and put it away.
lessons.homeConnection: Draw zigzags and waves in sand or with chalk at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make zigzag and wave patterns" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Copy my pattern
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will copy a simple pattern made of lines and circles.
successCriteria: Copies a line and circle pattern
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make marks with fingers, chalk and crayons and have been listening to the sounds s, a, t and p.
resources: A pattern card with a line and a circle
lessons.starter: Draw a line, a circle, a line, a circle. Say "I made a pattern. Can you copy it?"
teacherActivities: Draw a pattern slowly: line, circle, line, circle.
Say "Now you make it" and give each child a crayon.
learnerActivities: Children watch.
Child draws a pattern on paper.
Child says a word or shows.
Child shows their pattern to a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Draw a pattern slowly: line, circle, line, circle. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Now you make it" and give each child a crayon. Children: Child draws a pattern on paper.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Tell me about your pattern." Children: Child says a word or shows.
Step 4. Teacher: Display the patterns together. Children: Child shows their pattern to a friend.

practical.title: Pattern making
steps: Each child copies the pattern with a crayon.
Show the pattern to a friend.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic crayons and keep crayons out of mouths. Supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Draw the first part of the pattern and let the child continue.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a new pattern with three shapes.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Copies a simple pattern with support
lessons.conclusion: Hang the patterns on the wall and say "Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Draw a simple pattern at home and let your child copy it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "copy a simple pattern made of lines and circles" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 patterns check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child makes lines and patterns.
successCriteria: Makes straight and round marks on purpose
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make marks with fingers, chalk and crayons and have been listening to the sounds s, a, t and p.
lessons.starter: Draw a big line in the air and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: sand, paint and crayons.
At each station watch what marks the child makes.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every five minutes.
Child makes lines, circles and zigzags.
Children wash hands and tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: sand, paint and crayons. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch what marks the child makes. Children: Child makes lines, circles and zigzags.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Pattern stations
practical.safety: Supervise paint and sand closely. Use washable paint and wash hands after each station.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and offer one tool.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to make a pattern for friends to copy.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: makes straight lines; makes circles; copies a simple pattern.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
Makes lines and circles on purpose
lessons.homeConnection: Make patterns in sand or flour at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child makes lines and patterns" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
